bull_bear.body:
- No customer concentration — the Company states it is not reliant on revenues from transactions with any single external customer and does not receive 10% or more of its revenues from any single external customer
- Debt-free balance sheet — the Company states that Interest Coverage Ratio and Debt-Equity ratio are not relevant for it as it has no debt
- Branded heritage and leisure portfolio (WelcomHeritage) spread across multiple leisure destinations and states, including hill, desert, wildlife and lake destinations
- Group lineage and consolidated hospitality structure — hospitality entities previously held by ITC Limited were transferred to the Company on a going concern basis under the Scheme, giving it a ready subsidiary/associate platform including a Sri Lanka entity
- Two-tier governance structure with strategic supervision by the Board and executive management by the Strategic and Executive Management Committee, with day-to-day operational management of each hotel unit vested in its General Manager
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical conflict in West Asia disrupting travel demand — Travel activity during the year was impacted by geopolitical tensions and the West Asian conflict, which resulted in deferment of travel decisions and softer travel momentum; management cites geopolitical tensions, particularly in West Asia, as a key monitorable for the sector's near-term outlook.
- Elevated energy prices and inflation pressure on discretionary consumption — Supply-side disruption and elevated energy prices raise the risk of near-term inflationary pressures while weighing on private consumption and investor sentiment; global inflation is estimated to rise in 2026 primarily on higher energy and food prices — a direct pressure on discretionary travel spend.
- Elevated travel costs and macroeconomic uncertainty — Management flags elevated travel costs together with macroeconomic uncertainties as key monitorables for the sector's near-term outlook, alongside risks from persistent trade frictions.
- Aviation-related disruption and dependence on air connectivity — Travel activity was impacted by aviation-related disruptions during the year and domestic air passenger traffic grew only modestly Y-o-Y; the outlook for international tourism is explicitly tied to improved air connectivity.
- Adverse weather events affecting travel demand — Adverse weather events are named among the external developments that intermittently affected demand and deferred travel decisions during the year.
- New branded room supply, concentrated in the premium segment — Per Horwath HTL, branded hotel room supply expanded 7.8% Y-o-Y, with nearly 41% of the new supply added in 2025 pertaining to the premium (upscale and above) segment — the segment in which the Company competes — and the majority added outside the top ten markets.
- Slower global growth cycle — Global growth is projected to moderate to 3.1% in 2026 with only a modest recovery to 3.2% in 2027, with moderation in Emerging Markets — a softer backdrop for inbound and long-haul travel demand.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company operates in only one segment, i.e. 'Hotel Services', and its operations are primarily in India, with revenue reported on the basis of the location of the hotel property. Its portfolio includes WelcomHeritage-branded heritage hotels, resorts and spas located in leisure and heritage destinations across Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Karnataka and Maharashtra. Following the Scheme of Arrangement for demerger of the Hotels Business of ITC Limited into the Company (effective 1st January, 2025), ITC Limited's investments in hospitality entities such as Fortune Park Hotels Limited, Bay Islands Hotels Limited, Landbase India Limited, WelcomHotels Lanka (Private) Limited, Srinivasa Resorts Limited, International Travel House Limited, Gujarat Hotels Limited and Maharaja Heritage Resorts Limited were transferred to the Company on a going concern basis.

outlook.body: - The Company has a Dividend Distribution Policy, which is published on its website; the ordinary business of the 3rd Annual General Meeting includes declaration of a final dividend on equity shares for the financial year ended 31st March, 2026, with a record date fixed for determining member entitlement and a stated payment window in August 2026. On balance-sheet philosophy, the Company states that Interest Coverage Ratio and Debt-Equity ratio are not relevant for it as it has no debt. Governance of capital sits in a two-tier structure — strategic supervision by the Board, whose primary role is trusteeship to protect and enhance shareholder value across the Company and its wholly owned subsidiaries, and strategic/executive management by the Strategic and Executive Management Committee, which is also the Chief Operating Decision Maker responsible for allocating resources and assessing performance.

outlook.body: The routed sections contain no company-level capex, capacity-addition, commissioning or project-pipeline disclosure for ITC Hotels Limited — no new hotel, room addition, renovation or management-contract signing is described. The only Company footprint evidence in this text is a list of operating WelcomHeritage properties (Nos. 26-36 of a longer list) across Ranakpur, Ranikhet, Ranthambhore and Ratanpur in Rajasthan, Rishikesh and Ranikhet in Uttarakhand, Shimla and Solan in Himachal Pradesh, Srinagar in Jammu & Kashmir, Sandur in Karnataka and Tadoba (Chandrapur) in Maharashtra. Expansion context is stated only at INDUSTRY level: per Horwath HTL, the overall supply of branded hotel rooms across the country expanded by 7.8% Y-o-Y while demand grew at a higher pace of 9.1%, with nearly 41% of the new supply added in 2025 pertaining to the premium segment (upscale and above) and the majority of 2025 supply estimated to have been added outside India's top ten markets. Management describes the Indian hospitality industry as being at an inflection point, with large-scale investments in transport infrastructure expected to reshape travel over the medium term.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global economy backdrop: the global economy remained resilient and grew by 3.4% during the year (previous year 3.3%) amid heightened uncertainty and volatility, supported by technology-led investments, selective fiscal and monetary support and easing inflationary pressures
- As per IMF estimates, global growth is projected to moderate to 3.1% in 2026 with a modest recovery to 3.2% in 2027; the outlook reflects stable growth in Advanced Economies and a moderation in Emerging Markets
- Global inflation is estimated to rise to 4.4% in 2026 from 4.1% in 2025, primarily driven by higher energy and food prices
- India reaffirmed its status as the fastest growing major economy with 7.6% growth in Real GDP, up from 7.1% in FY 2024-25, with domestic demand continuing to anchor growth
- Indian demand drivers cited: supportive fiscal and monetary policies, reduced income tax rates, GST rate rationalization across sectors and benign inflation levels; services and manufacturing grew 9% and 11.5% respectively over the previous year
- Watch-item on demand: since March 2026 the West Asia conflict has emerged as a significant source of uncertainty, with supply-side disruption and elevated energy prices raising near-term inflation risk while weighing on private consumption and investor sentiment
- Escalation of geopolitical tensions in West Asia from February-March 2026 led to heightened energy market volatility and further weighed on trade sentiment, alongside risks from elevated inflation and persistent trade frictions
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
